{"id": "98fbde10-d6e2-41b0-91c5-22f68a24830c", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_PHxyyP2SB2h5g9kQq988Kn", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"---\\\\nname: ec2-patch-windows-servicing-store\\\\ndescription: >-\\\\n  Recover a Windows Server (2012 R2, 2016, 2019, 2022, 2025) EC2 instance whose\\\\n  patching is blocked by a component-servicing fault \\\\u2014 the family of failures\\\\n  rooted in CBS/WinSxS, the servicing stack (SSU), pending servicing\\\\n  transactions, the Windows Update datastore, or a stalled feature update. Use\\\\n  when a patch or Windows Update install fails with 0x80073712, 0x800F0831\\\\n  (CBS_E_STORE_CORRUPTION), 0x800F081F, 0x800F0922, 0x80073701, 0x80070BC9,\\\\n  0x8024400A/0x80244010, or 0xC1900101; when DISM/ScanHealth reports corruption\\\\n  or \\\\\"packages are pending servicing\\\\\"; when updates stick in\\\\n  \\\\\"InstalledPendingReboot\\\\\"/\\\\\"Pending Install\\\\\"; when DataStore.edb is oversized; or\\\\n  when Windows.old lingers after a failed in-place upgrade. Instance is Online in SSM.\\\\nIf the failure is a *connectivity* fault (WSUS/TLS/proxy) or a *policy* blocker\\\\n(GPO/AV/BitLocker), this is the wrong skill \\\\u2014 those are separate domains.\\\\n\\\\n## The key insight: diagnose the sub-fault first \\\\u2014 they masquerade as each other\\\\n`0x800F0831` / \\\\\"store corruption\\\\\" is the most common *surface* symptom, but its\\\\n*cause* is often not store corruption at all:\\\\n- an **outdated servicing stack (SSU)** can\\'t process a new LCU manifest \\\\u2192 surfaces as store corruption;\\\\n- a **halted pending transaction** (interrupted reboot) \\\\u2192 surfaces as store corruption;\\\\n- a **stalled feature update** leaves mixed package state \\\\u2192 LCU \\\\\"not applicable\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\nRunning `DISM /RestoreHealth` blindly loops for hours when the real cause is a\\\\nstale SSU or a pending transaction. **Identify the sub-fault, then apply the\\\\nmatching path in the correct order.**\\\\n\\\\n## Diagnosis first (always)\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Capture the failing error code and the servicing state before changing anything:\\\\n  ```powershell\\\\n  DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth\\\\n  DISM /Online /Get-Packages /Format:Table | Select-String \\\\\"Pending\\\\\"\\\\n  Test-Path \\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\servicing\\\\\\\\Packages\\\\\\\\pending.xml\\\\\"\\\\n  (Get-Item \\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\SoftwareDistribution\\\\\\\\DataStore\\\\\\\\DataStore.edb\\\\\").Length/1MB\\\\n  Get-ChildItem \\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\Windows.old\\\\\",\\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\`$WINDOWS.~BT\\\\\" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\\\\n  Get-Content \\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\Logs\\\\\\\\CBS\\\\\\\\CBS.log\\\\\" -Tail 80 | Select-String \\\\\"ERROR|corrupt|pending|missing\\\\\"\\\\n  ```\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Route to the sub-fault by signature (load the matching reference for exact steps):\\\\n  - Pending transactions present (`pending.xml`, \\\\\"Install Pending\\\\\", `0x800F0922`) \\\\u2192 read [pending transactions](reference/pending-transactions.md) \\\\u2014 clear these BEFORE any DISM repair.\\\\n  - SSU outdated / `0x80070BC9` / `0x80073701` on LCU \\\\u2192 read [SSU ordering](reference/ssu-ordering.md) \\\\u2014 install SSU BEFORE the LCU and before RestoreHealth.\\\\n  - Genuine CBS/WinSxS corruption (`0x80073712`, `0x800F0831` with no pending/SSU cause) \\\\u2192 read [CBS store repair](reference/cbs-store-repair.md).\\\\n  - WU datastore bloat/corruption (`0x8024400A`, `DataStore.edb` >1GB, ESENT 455/489) \\\\u2192 read [WU datastore](reference/wu-datastore.md).\\\\n  - Stalled feature update (`0xC1900101`, lingering `Windows.old`) \\\\u2192 read [feature update state](reference/feature-update.md).\\\\n\\\\n## Ordered recovery (dependencies matter \\\\u2014 do not reorder)\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: **Clear pending transactions first.** `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RevertPendingActions`;\\\\n  rename a stale (`>24h`) `pending.xml`; clear `SessionsPending`. A pending transaction poisons every later step.\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: **Bring the servicing stack current.** Install any pending Servicing Stack Update BEFORE the LCU.\\\\n  An old SSU cannot process a new LCU manifest and will re-manifest as store corruption.\\\\n- [ ] Step 5: **Repair the component store** only after 3\\\\u20134: `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`\\\\n  (add `/Source:WIM:<path>\\\\\\\\install.wim:<idx> /LimitAccess` on isolated fleets where WU is blocked), then `sfc /scannow`.\\\\n- [ ] Step 6: **Reset WU components** if the datastore is implicated: stop `wuauserv,cryptSvc,bits,msiserver`;\\\\n  rename `SoftwareDistribution` and `catroot2`; restart. See the datastore reference for the `DataStore.edb` specifics.\\\\n- [ ] Step 7: **Reboot** to let TrustedInstaller finalize valid pending operations, then re-scan.\\\\n\\\\n## Validation (check your own work before reporting success)\\\\nDo not report the instance patchable until you confirm each of these:\\\\n- [ ] `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth` reports the store **healthy** (not just \\\\\"RestoreHealth exit 0\\\\\").\\\\n- [ ] No packages remain \\\\\"Install Pending\\\\\"/\\\\\"Uninstall Pending\\\\\" and `pending.xml` is absent.\\\\n- [ ] No Servicing Stack Update is still pending (`Search(\\\\\"IsInstalled=0\\\\\")` returns no \\\\\"Servicing Stack\\\\\" title).\\\\n- [ ] The original failing update/patch scan re-run no longer returns its original error code.\\\\n- [ ] `wuauserv` is Running.\\\\nIf any check fails, consult the matching reference\\'s escalation section rather than re-looping DISM.\\\\n\\\\n## Gotchas\\\\n- **SSU installs are forward-only \\\\u2014 they cannot be uninstalled.** Do not promise a rollback of the servicing stack.\\\\n- **Order is load-bearing:** pending-transaction clear \\\\u2192 SSU \\\\u2192 RestoreHealth \\\\u2192 SFC \\\\u2192 reboot. SFC before a healthy store just fails; RestoreHealth before clearing a pending transaction loops.\\\\n- **A recent `pending.xml` (<24h) may be valid** \\\\u2014 renaming it can abort a legitimate in-flight servicing operation. Check age first.\\\\n- **`/Source` build must match the running OS build exactly** (`Version` + UBR); a mismatched WIM fails RestoreHealth with a generic error.\\\\n- **On an isolated/patched fleet, WU as the RestoreHealth source is blocked** \\\\u2014 supply an explicit `/Source` with `/LimitAccess` or the repair silently retries WU and times out.\\\\n- **A stalled feature update is NOT store corruption** \\\\u2014 running RestoreHealth against a half-upgraded image (\\\\\"not applicable to this image\\\\\") wastes the maintenance window; resolve the upgrade state first.\\\\n\", \"resource_manifest\": [\"SKILL.md\", \"automation/iam-policy.json\", \"reference/pending-transactions.md\", \"reference/wu-datastore.md\", \"reference/feature-update.md\", \"reference/ssu-ordering.md\", \"reference/cbs-store-repair.md\"]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "7a34516c-c753-4ace-af54-7d4d7a0a3e27", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_SOjamF5sgjKqxHID1nNFsz", "content": "[{'text': '# Pending servicing transactions (clear BEFORE any DISM repair)\\n\\n**Signatures:** `0x800F0922` (CBS_E_INSTALLERS_FAILED), `0x800F081F` (CBS_E_SOURCE_MISSING),\\n`0x800F0831` with pending references; DISM \"packages are pending servicing\"; CBS.log\\n\"transaction halted\"/\"pending.xml\"; boot slow while TrustedInstaller retries.\\n\\n**Why first:** a halted transaction poisons SSU installs and RestoreHealth alike \u2014 both will\\nloop or fail until the transaction is reverted or completed.\\n\\n## Steps\\n1. Identify pending operations and the marker file:\\n   ```powershell\\n   DISM /Online /Get-Packages /Format:Table | Select-String \"Pending\"\\n   Test-Path \"$env:SystemRoot\\\\servicing\\\\Packages\\\\pending.xml\"\\n   ```\\n2. Revert pending actions:\\n   ```powershell\\n   DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RevertPendingActions\\n   ```\\n3. Rename `pending.xml` ONLY if stale (>24h) \u2014 a recent one may be a valid in-flight operation:\\n   ```powershell\\n   $x=\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\servicing\\\\Packages\\\\pending.xml\"\\n   if((Test-Path $x) -and (((Get-Date)-(Get-Item $x).LastWriteTime).TotalHours -gt 24)){Rename-Item $x \"$x.bak_$(Get-Date -Format yyyyMMdd)\" -Force}\\n   ```\\n4. Clear orphaned session state:\\n   ```powershell\\n   Stop-Service wuauserv,TrustedInstaller -Force -EA SilentlyContinue\\n   Remove-Item \\'HKLM:\\\\SOFTWARE\\\\Microsoft\\\\Windows\\\\CurrentVersion\\\\Component Based Servicing\\\\SessionsPending\\' -Recurse -Force -EA SilentlyContinue\\n   Start-Service TrustedInstaller -EA SilentlyContinue\\n   ```\\n5. **Reboot** \u2014 some transactions can only finalize during boot.\\n\\n## Escalation\\n- Boot loop from a pending transaction \u2192 boot Safe Mode (`bcdedit /set {default} safeboot minimal`) then RevertPendingActions.\\n- Specific stuck package \u2192 `DISM /Online /Remove-Package /PackageName:<name>`.\\n- Rollback: restore the renamed `pending.xml.bak_*` if a revert removed a valid operation.\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_N5vCeUzsu742PDpW48nznh", "content": "[{'text': '# Servicing Stack Update (SSU) ordering (install BEFORE the LCU)\\n\\n**Signatures:** `0x80070BC9` (ERROR_FAIL_NOACTION_REBOOT), `0x80073701`\\n(ERROR_SXS_ASSEMBLY_MISSING) on LCU; CBS.log \"Servicing stack must be updated before this\\npackage can be installed\"; LCU downloads then fails at \"Installing\"; Server 2016 stuck on old CU.\\n\\n**Why:** the servicing stack is what *processes* update manifests. An outdated SSU cannot parse a\\nnewer LCU manifest, and the failure surfaces as store corruption \u2014 so RestoreHealth \"fixes\"\\nnothing. SSU must be current first.\\n\\n## Steps\\n1. Report OS build + servicing stack:\\n   ```powershell\\n   $os=Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem\\n   \"$($os.Caption) Build $($os.BuildNumber).$((Get-ItemProperty \\'HKLM:\\\\SOFTWARE\\\\Microsoft\\\\Windows NT\\\\CurrentVersion\\').UBR)\"\\n   ```\\n2. Find pending SSU vs LCU (SSU installs separately on 2016; combined on 2019+):\\n   ```powershell\\n   $s=(New-Object -ComObject Microsoft.Update.Session).CreateUpdateSearcher().Search(\"IsInstalled=0 and Type=\\'Software\\'\").Updates\\n   $s|?{$_.Title -match \\'Servicing Stack\\'}|%{ \"SSU: $($_.Title)\" }\\n   ```\\n3. Install the SSU first (download+install just the \"Servicing Stack\" updates via\\n   `Microsoft.Update.Session`; ResultCode 2=Succeeded, 3=SucceededWithErrors), then let the LCU proceed.\\n4. Re-evaluate the component store: `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup`.\\n5. Verify no SSU remains pending before installing the LCU.\\n\\n## Escalation\\n- Server 2012 R2: download SSU from Microsoft Update Catalog, install via `wusa.exe`; SHA-2 chain may be required.\\n- Server 2016: specific LCUs require a specific SSU version \u2014 check the KB prerequisites.\\n- WSUS: ensure the SSU (not just the LCU) is approved.\\n- 2019+: ensure the combined SSU+LCU package is being offered.\\n- Since 2024, a SafeOS/WinRE update may also be required.\\n- **SSU is forward-only \u2014 it cannot be uninstalled.**\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_SLYPOvgv05bAmebnZfCf4E", "content": "[{'text': '# CBS / WinSxS component store repair (only after pending + SSU are handled)\\n\\n**Signatures:** `0x80073712` (\"component store corrupted\"), `0x800F0831`\\n(CBS_E_STORE_CORRUPTION) with no pending-transaction or SSU cause, `0x800736B3`\\n(\"referenced assembly not installed\"), Error 14098; DISM ScanHealth reports corruption;\\nCBS.log \"store corruption\"/\"manifest missing\".\\n\\n**Preconditions:** pending transactions cleared, SSU current, \u22655 GB free on C:.\\n\\n## Steps\\n1. Assess: `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth`.\\n2. Repair: `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`.\\n   - On an isolated/patched fleet WU is blocked as the repair source \u2014 supply an explicit source:\\n     `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth /Source:WIM:<path>\\\\install.wim:<idx> /LimitAccess`.\\n   - **`/Source` build must match the running OS build+UBR exactly** or RestoreHealth fails generically.\\n3. System files: `sfc /scannow` (only after the store is healthy \u2014 SFC uses the store to repair).\\n4. If WU components are implicated, reset them:\\n   ```powershell\\n   Stop-Service wuauserv,cryptSvc,bits,msiserver -Force -EA SilentlyContinue\\n   Rename-Item \"$env:SystemRoot\\\\SoftwareDistribution\" \"$env:SystemRoot\\\\SoftwareDistribution.old\" -Force -EA SilentlyContinue\\n   Rename-Item \"$env:SystemRoot\\\\System32\\\\catroot2\" \"$env:SystemRoot\\\\System32\\\\catroot2.old\" -Force -EA SilentlyContinue\\n   Start-Service wuauserv,cryptSvc,bits,msiserver -EA SilentlyContinue\\n   ```\\n5. Verify: `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth` reports **healthy**.\\n\\n## Rollback\\nRestore `SoftwareDistribution.old` / `catroot2.old` if the reset caused a regression.\\n\\n## Escalation\\n- RestoreHealth still fails \u2192 confirm WU reachability or supply `/Source`; read CBS.log for the exact missing manifest.\\n- Severe corruption \u2192 in-place upgrade repair or rebuild from AMI.\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "f7fc49d9-d612-4624-807d-68a9f2e70b4d", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Got it — thanks for the detail. Here's the thing: the fact that `/RestoreHealth` keeps looping *without converging* even after two runs is itself the key signal. On Server 2016 specifically, that pattern is almost always caused by one of two things masquerading as store corruption, not genuine CBS damage — and running RestoreHealth blindly a third time won't fix either.

**Don't run `/RestoreHealth` again yet.** Diagnose first:

### 1. Check for a halted pending transaction (highest priority — this poisons everything downstream)
```powershell
DISM /Online /Get-Packages /Format:Table | Select-String "Pending"
Test-Path "$env:SystemRoot\servicing\Packages\pending.xml"
```
If a pending transaction exists, clear it **before** anything else:
```powershell
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RevertPendingActions
# only rename pending.xml if it's >24h old — check timestamp first, a fresh one may be legitimate
```
Then clear orphaned session state and **reboot** — some transactions only finalize at boot.

### 2. Check for an outdated Servicing Stack Update (SSU) — very common on 2016
Server 2016 ships SSU separately from the LCU (unlike 2019+). An old SSU can't parse a newer LCU manifest, and that failure surfaces as "store corruption" even though the store is fine:
```powershell
$s = (New-Object -ComObject Microsoft.Update.Session).CreateUpdateSearcher().Search("IsInstalled=0 and Type='Software'").Updates
$s | ?{$_.Title -match 'Servicing Stack'} | %{ "SSU: $($_.Title)" }
```
If a Servicing Stack Update is pending, install **that first**, separately, before letting the cumulative update retry. SSUs are forward-only (can't be uninstalled), but that's expected and fine.

### 3. Only then, repair the store
Once pending transactions are cleared and the SSU is current:
```powershell
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
sfc /scannow
```
If this instance is on an isolated/patched fleet where Windows Update is blocked as a source, RestoreHealth will silently retry WU and time out — in that case supply `/Source:WIM:<path>\install.wim:<idx> /LimitAccess` with a WIM matching the exact build + UBR.

### 4. Reboot, then validate — don't just trust exit code 0
```powershell
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth
```
Confirm: store reports healthy, no packages "Install Pending", no SSU still pending, `wuauserv` running, and the original cumulative update re-run no longer throws `0x80073712`.

Want me to pull the CBS.log tail and current package/SSU state from this instance via SSM to confirm which of the two (pending transaction vs. stale SSU) is actually in play here, rather than guessing?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
